goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — An unavailable RSS feed aborts retrieval before the HTTP fallback, leaving otherwise reachable articles stuck on the loading screen.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 35-47, the perform_retrieve method first checks if feed_polling_enabled? and calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the poll_feed method uses SimpleRSS.parse with open() which can raise exceptions if the feed URL is unavailable or malformed. If this raises an exception, the code never reaches the fetch_http fallback on line 51. This means if RSS polling is enabled but the feed is temporarily unavailable, articles that could be retrieved via HTTP will be stuck on the loading screen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — Concurrent feed imports can save body B followed by hash A, causing later imports of A to skip correction and leave the wrong article content indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the import method in topic_embed.rb lines 30-40, when updating an existing embed: (1) content_sha1 is computed from new contents, (2) revisor.revise! updates the post with new contents, (3) embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) saves the hash. If two concurrent imports happen with different content, there's a race condition where: Thread A computes hash_A, Thread B computes hash_B, Thread A revises post to content_A, Thread B revises post to content_B, Thread A saves hash_A, Thread B saves hash_B. Now the database has content_B but hash_A. Future imports of content_A will see hash matches and skip update, leaving wrong content. This is a real concurrency bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Removing the public `--category`/`-c` option makes existing import invocations fail and prevents callers from preserving their target category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of `method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: 'The category to post in'` at line 117 of the original file, and the removal of the code that used it (`category_id = nil; if options[:category]; category_id = Category.where(name: options[:category]).first.try(:id); end`). This is a breaking change - existing scripts or documentation that use `--category` or `-c` flags will fail when invoking this import command. The finding correctly identifies that this removes a public CLI option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — URL rewriting converts protocol-relative CDN URLs into paths on the article host and leaves document-relative URLs unresolved, breaking imported images and links.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-71, the code only handles URLs that start_with?('/') - meaning it only converts absolute paths (like '/hello') to full URLs. The code does NOT handle: 1) Protocol-relative URLs (starting with '//') which would not match start_with?('/') after the first character check fails, and 2) Document-relative URLs (like 'images/wat.jpg' without leading slash) which are completely ignored. This is a real bug - protocol-relative CDN URLs like '//cdn.example.com/image.jpg' would pass through unchanged (which might be okay), but document-relative URLs would remain broken. The finding correctly identifies that the URL rewriting is incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Reading only `i.content.scrub` fails on valid RSS entries that provide description or content:encoded instead, aborting feed import.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment - that reading only `i.content.scrub` fails when RSS entries don't have a content field and instead use description or content:encoded. Both issues point to the same bug: the code assumes `i.content` is always populated, but many RSS feeds use alternative fields like description, leading to failures. The candidate mentions 'aborting feed import' which is essentially the same consequence as the 'nil pointer exception' mentioned in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — TopicEmbed.import mutates its caller-owned contents string, so reusing an input instance silently changes later imports; build the attributed content in a new string.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, the code does `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` which mutates the input string parameter in place using `<<`. If a caller passes the same string object to multiple calls of `import`, the string would accumulate the footer content from each call. This is a real mutation bug - the method modifies caller-owned data. However, examining the actual callers in the diff (poll_feed.rb and topic_retriever.rb via import_remote), each call creates a fresh content string, so the bug may not manifest in practice. Still, it's a genuine code defect that could cause issues if the API is used differently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key and its digest dependency are dead code because no polling path ever reads the computed key.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, `feed_key` method is defined at lines 20-22 in poll_feed.rb but is never called anywhere in the file or elsewhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method doesn't use `feed_key`. This is dead code that was introduced but never utilized. While not a bug (the code works without it), it's a legitimate code quality issue - unused code that should either be removed or actually used for its intended purpose (likely caching/throttling feed modifications).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Reading the entire remote article without a byte limit can exhaust a worker's memory on a large response.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code calls `open(url).read` without any byte limit when fetching remote content. This is visible in the diff: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. A malicious or unexpectedly large remote page could cause the worker to consume excessive memory, potentially leading to denial of service. This is a real security/resource exhaustion concern introduced by this new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every distinct cache miss reparses and imports the full feed item by item, multiplying network, parsing, and database work under concurrent misses.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 33-46, the `perform_retrieve` method checks if a TopicEmbed exists, then calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` which processes ALL feed items (see app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 27-35 iterating through `rss.items.each`). The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` (lines 22-31) uses Redis setnx with 60-second expiry, but this only prevents the same URL from being retrieved twice within 60 seconds. If multiple different URLs have cache misses concurrently, each will trigger a full feed poll. This is a legitimate scalability/efficiency concern about the design, though not a correctness bug - the code will work, just inefficiently under concurrent load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — The importer records the new content hash even when PostRevisor#revise! returns false, permanently suppressing retries while leaving the embedded post stale.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-37, when updating an existing embed: the code calls `revisor.revise!()` and then unconditionally calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` regardless of whether revise! succeeded. If revise! returns false (fails), the content_sha1 is still updated to the new value, which means future import attempts will see matching hashes and skip the update, leaving the post with stale content permanently. The code should check the return value of revise! before updating the hash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — A feed item without a content field raises on nil.scrub and, with job retries disabled, lets one persistent malformed item prevent every later item from being imported.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item doesn't have a 'content' field, `i.content` would be nil, and calling `.scrub` on nil would raise a NoMethodError. The job has `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 12), so this error would not be retried. Since this happens inside `rss.items.each`, one malformed item would cause the entire job to fail, preventing subsequent items from being processed. This is a real bug - the code doesn't handle the case where content might be nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — HTML-unescaping feed content and importing it as unsanitized raw HTML turns escaped scripts or event handlers into stored XSS on the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. Looking at TopicEmbed.import in topic_embed.rb, the content is passed to PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without sanitization: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This means HTML-unescaped content from RSS feeds (which could contain escaped malicious scripts like `<script>`) gets unescaped by CGI.unescapeHTML and then rendered as raw HTML without sanitization, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Following redirects without revalidating their destinations lets an allowed-host redirect bypass the embed host check and fetch internal HTTP resources.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a security issue in TopicEmbed.import_remote at line 48, which uses `open(url).read` via ruby-readability. The code only validates the embeddable_host setting against the initial URL in TopicRetriever.invalid_host?, but if the allowed host redirects to an internal resource, the open() call will follow that redirect without revalidation. This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability where an attacker controlling content on the allowed embeddable_host could redirect to internal services (e.g., http://localhost, http://169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata). The diff shows this is a real security concern in the newly added embedding functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The no-embed example expects the removed synchronous TopicRetriever call, so it fails against the new enqueue path and never verifies the loading response or job arguments.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the test 'expects the removed synchronous TopicRetriever call' but looking at the diff, the test at lines 41-47 in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb actually does test the new enqueue path correctly. It expects TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed to return nil, then expects TopicRetriever.new to return a mock retriever, and expects retrieve to be called on it. The test is testing the synchronous TopicRetriever.retrieve call that happens in the controller, not a removed path. Looking at embed_controller.rb, when topic_id is nil, it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading'. The test mocks TopicRetriever directly, but the actual controller code uses Jobs.enqueue. However, the test does pass because it's mocking at the TopicRetriever level. The finding's claim about 'removed synchronous TopicRetriever call' is incorrect - the controller uses Jobs.enqueue, and the test mocks TopicRetriever which would be called by the job, not directly by the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — The valid-host examples stub retrieved_recently? itself, leaving the real Redis throttle, expiry, and no_throttle branches completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb stubs `retrieved_recently?` in the 'valid host' context (lines 35 and 41), which means the actual Redis throttle implementation in lib/topic_retriever.rb (lines 23-32 showing $redis.setnx and $redis.expire logic, plus the no_throttle option) is never exercised by these tests. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic - the Redis-based throttling mechanism with its 60-second expiry and the no_throttle bypass option are real functionality that lacks test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — Every poll-feed example mocks poll_feed, so no test exercises RSS parsing, link-to-id fallback, missing-user handling, or TopicEmbed import.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the execute method's guard conditions and delegates to poll_feed via mocking. Looking at the diff, the actual poll_feed method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb contains significant logic: user lookup, RSS parsing with SimpleRSS, link/id fallback for URLs, content unescaping, and TopicEmbed.import calls. None of this is tested because all specs mock poll_feed. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — The new RetrieveTopic job has no tests for missing embed_url, user lookup, or the staff throttle-bypass option passed to TopicRetriever.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new RetrieveTopic job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) lacks dedicated unit tests. Looking at the diff, the job has specific logic: it raises an error if embed_url is missing, looks up a user by id, and passes no_throttle based on user.try(:staff?). While there are tests for TopicRetriever (spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb) and PollFeed (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb), there is no corresponding spec/jobs/retrieve_topic_spec.rb in the diff. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial job logic.
